Integration Against the Density as the Expected Derivative

Source: R/expect_method.R
expect_integrate.Rd

Selects numerical integration over the response as the method that obtains an expected derivative. The quantity integrated against the density \(f\) is the one that identity names: $$\mathbb{E}[\partial^k \ell] = \int \partial^k \ell(y;\theta)\, f(y;\theta)\,dy \quad \text{for } \texttt{identity = "hessian"},$$ the observed derivative of the requested order, or $$-\sum_{\pi} \int \prod_{B \in \pi} \ell_B(y;\theta)\,f(y;\theta)\,dy \quad \text{for } \texttt{identity = "score"},$$ where \(\pi\) runs over the partitions of the index set into at least two blocks and \(\ell_B\) is the derivative of the log-density with respect to the parameters indexed by the block \(B\) (the Bartlett partition identity; at order 2 it reads \(-\int \ell_i \ell_j f\,dy\)). The integrals are computed by batched adaptive quadrature for a continuous family and by series summation for a discrete one. The computation is deterministic. The accuracy of the quadrature and of the series is set by the arguments of the constructor, whose defaults are those of numericals7::quad_vec() and numericals7::series_vec().

With identity = "hessian" the integral needs the derivative of the target order and costs one integral per component; it is normally the most accurate method when that derivative is available in closed form. With identity = "score" the target order is never needed, only the lower ones, and the cost is one integral per partition and component. The score identity is the one that remains valid when the log-likelihood has a kink in a parameter: at order 2, for a family with a non-smooth parameter (see param_smoothness()), the observed second derivative lacks the point mass at the kink, and identity = "hessian" signals an error that names identity = "score".

With the defaults this is the method that distrib_deriv3() and distrib_deriv4() use for an expected derivative when method is NULL.

Usage

expect_integrate(
  identity = c("hessian", "score"),
  quad_atol = 1e-10,
  quad_rtol = 1e-08,
  max_panels = 4096L,
  series_atol = 1e-12,
  series_rtol = 1e-10,
  max_terms = 100000L
)

Arguments

identity

One of "hessian" (the default) and "score". See the description and expected_derivative_methods.

quad_atol, quad_rtol

The absolute and the relative tolerance of the quadrature of a continuous family, single positive finite numbers. A panel of the integration is accepted when its error estimate is below quad_atol + quad_rtol * abs(integral). The defaults are 1e-10 and 1e-8.

max_panels

The largest number of panels that the quadrature of one parameter configuration may reach, a single positive finite number. A row that needs more panels is not accepted by the batched quadrature and is integrated by the scalar integrator of stats. The default is 4096.

series_atol, series_rtol

The absolute and the relative tolerance of the series summation of a discrete family, single positive finite numbers. The defaults are 1e-12 and 1e-10.

max_terms

The largest number of terms of a series, a single positive finite number. A series that has not met its tolerance after that many terms signals an error. The default is 100000.

Value

An S7 object of class ExpectIntegrate, which inherits from ExpectMethod, with the properties identity, quad_atol, quad_rtol, max_panels, series_atol, series_rtol and max_terms.

See also

expect_opg() and expect_mc() for the other methods; expected_derivative_methods for the comparison; distrib_deriv3(), distrib_deriv4() and distrib_expected_hessian() for the functions that take the object.

Examples

Dens <- S7::new_class("DensIntegrate", parent = continuous_distrib)
S7::method(distrib_pdf, Dens) <- function(distrib, y, theta, log = FALSE, ...) {
  stats::dnorm(y, theta[[1]], theta[[2]], log = log)
}
d <- Dens(distrib_name = "dens", dimension = "univariate",
          bounds = c(-Inf, Inf), params = c("mu", "sigma"),
          params_interpretation = c(mu = "location", sigma = "scale"),
          n_params = 2L,
          params_bounds = list(mu = c(-Inf, Inf), sigma = c(0, Inf)),
          link_params = list(mu = linkfunctions7::identity_link(),
                             sigma = linkfunctions7::log_link()),
          params_smooth = c(mu = TRUE, sigma = TRUE))
th <- list(mu = 0, sigma = 2)
# The expected information of sigma is 2 / sigma^2 = 0.5 in absolute value,
# by either identity.
distrib_expected_hessian(d, 0, th, method = expect_integrate())$sigma_sigma
#> [1] -0.5
distrib_expected_hessian(d, 0, th,
                         method = expect_integrate(identity = "score"))$sigma_sigma
#> [1] -0.5

# Tighter tolerances for the quadrature are set in the object.
a <- expect_integrate(quad_atol = 1e-12, quad_rtol = 1e-10)
a
#> Expectation by integration against the density (quad_atol = 0.000000000001, quad_rtol = 0.0000000001)
distrib_expected_hessian(d, 0, th, method = a)$sigma_sigma
#> [1] -0.5
